newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AWB Report-Rain downgrades Australian wheat.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AWB Report-Rain downgrades Australian wheat.

text.p: Rain interrupted the Australian harvest in three states during the past week, the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said in its weekly grain market report.

There were reports of some downgrading in northern parts of Western Australia (WA) but harvest had still not restarted generally in northern New South Wales and the AWB had no indication of any damage, it said.
Rain was falling late in the week in southern areas of WA, it said.

Milling wheat prices in general reacted to the A$15.00 a tonne reduction in estimated pool return with a fall of about A$4.00 to A$5.00 a tonne, though some confidence may be starting to come into the domestic market on the back of the pool harvest payment, it said.
Feed grain prices continued to fall with barley and sorghum dropping by about A$2.00 a tonne and feed wheat by A$5.00 a tonne, it said.
The AWB's indicator price for wheat delivered Newcastle rose by A$1.00 a tonne to A$126.75 over the week.
The AWB has held its estimate of the national wheat crop at 21 million tonnes.
On the international market, AWB said the European Union (EU) again lifted the subsidy it offered on wheat exports during the week to A$33.00 a tonne on 325,000 tonnes of wheat to open destinations.
This priced EU wheat at about A$186.00 a tonne, it said.
Argentina continued to be an aggressive marketer with a sale at A$151.00 during the week and offers of wheat for delivery April to June at A$170.00 a tonne.
The condition of the U.S. winter wheat crop continued to improve with 85 percent of the crop now emerged and rated in good to excellent condition, it said.

In Canada, reports of damage to the crop continued to surface with a grade split for the Saskatchewan spring wheat crop showing 38 percent downgraded to number three or four grade and about 600,000 hectares of wheat, mostly weather damaged, still to harvest, it said.
